introduction.text: In this lesson, you will learn how to use the preterite tense to talk about actions that happened in the past. You will focus on regular verbs and get familiar with their conjugation patterns.
introduction.culturalNote: In many Spanish-speaking countries, storytelling about the past is an important tradition, often shared during family gatherings.

vocabulary.definition: A word that describes an action.
vocabulary.tip: Remember that verbs are essential for forming sentences.

vocabulary.definition: To communicate or express thoughts verbally.

exampleSentence.translation: Yesterday I talked with my friend.

vocabulary.tip: This is a common verb used in everyday conversations.
Use this verb to discuss meals and dining experiences.

vocabulary.definition: To have residence in a place.
vocabulary.tip: This verb is useful when talking about where you are from.

exampleSentence.translation: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

vocabulary.tip: Use this word to refer to past events.

exampleSentence.translation: Last night I saw a movie.

vocabulary.tip: Great for discussing events that happened after sunset.

grammar.title: Preterite Tense: Regular Verbs
grammar.explanation: The preterite tense is used to describe completed actions in the past. Regular verbs follow specific patterns: -ar verbs end in -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron; -er/-ir verbs end in -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron.

rows: hablar: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablaron
comer: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comieron

examples.breakdown: Yo (I) + hablé (talked) is the first person preterite form.
Tú (You) + comiste (ate) is the second person preterite form.

commonMistakes: Confusing preterite with imperfect: Remember that preterite is for completed actions, while imperfect is for ongoing or habitual actions.
Using incorrect endings: Make sure to use the right endings for each verb type.

dialogue.title: Talking About Yesterday
dialogue.context: Two friends discussing their previous day at a café.

lines.translation: What did you do yesterday, Sofia?
Yesterday I went to the market.
Yes, I bought fruits and vegetables.

lines.text: ¡Qué bien! Yo comí en un restaurante.
lines.translation: How nice! I ate at a restaurant.
I went to 'The House of Tacos'.

culture.title: Storytelling in Latin America
culture.text: In Latin America, storytelling is a vibrant part of culture, often shared during family meals or community gatherings. People enjoy recounting past experiences, using the preterite tense to engage listeners.
culture.funFact: In some countries, it's common to have a 'storyteller' during gatherings who shares family history and traditions.

keyPoints: The preterite tense is used for completed actions in the past.
Regular -ar, -er, and -ir verbs have specific conjugation patterns.
Use time expressions like 'ayer' (yesterday) to indicate when the action happened.
Practice by talking about your own past experiences.
summary.nextSteps: Practice conjugating regular verbs in the preterite tense and create sentences about your past activities.
